subtype: Approach: revising categories after an income change [Revision]
passage: When Omkar's raise arrived, the first thing Jasleen noticed was how fast the ideas came: a bigger flat, a new car, a holiday abroad. A showroom in town had an offer ending on Saturday, which made everything feel urgent. "Let's not touch the spending plan tonight," said Jasleen. "Let's sleep on it and rewrite it on Sunday." They sat down with the old sheet after the offer had expired. The extra money went into three parts: a higher amount to savings, a small upgrade to their own life, and a fund for sending money to Omkar's parents every month. "The upgrade first is a better mattress," Jasleen said, laughing, and wrote it down. The car offer passed. Neither of them missed it.

qa.q: What were the three parts the extra income was split into?
qa.a: A higher amount to savings, a small upgrade to their own life, and a fund for sending money to Omkar's parents.

qa.q: What was Jasleen feeling about the showroom's deadline?
qa.a: Jasleen was wary of the false urgency and wanted to stay calm, choosing to sleep on it first.

qa.q: What could they do if Omkar's parents' needs change later?
qa.a: They could review the size of the fund as part of the monthly plan and change it together.

qa.q: How might Omkar's parents see the new fund?
qa.a: They may feel grateful and relieved, and perhaps a little uneasy about receiving money.

grounding: After a raise, Jasleen and Omkar resist raising spending, split it into savings, a small upgrade and a parents' fund, and rewrite the plan.

subtype: Approach: revising categories after an income change [Revision]
passage:
The raise letter arrived on a Tuesday, and by Tuesday evening Bidisha had three new tabs open: a bigger flat in Salt Lake, a new phone, a weekend in Darjeeling. Her sister Usha, who shared the flat and the budget sheet with her, closed the laptop gently.
"Before we spend it twice over, let's look at the plan," Usha said.
They sat on the floor with tea. The old plan was built for the old salary. Bidisha frowned. "If we just upgrade everything, we'll be exactly as stretched as before, only fancier."
So they rewrote it in three parts. A bigger slice went to savings. A small part became "nice things", which meant the new phone, but in March. And a new line: Ma and Baba, for their medicines and the house repairs, sent on the 5th of each month.
Bidisha grumbled about the phone waiting. But she was the one who labelled the new line.

qa.q: On which day each month will the Ma and Baba money be sent?
What does Bidisha's grumbling about the phone suggest she feels?
qa.a: Bidisha is a little disappointed to wait, but still committed, since she labelled the new line herself.

qa.q: Which part of the rewrite would you keep if the next raise were smaller?
qa.a: The three-part split, even with smaller amounts, so extra money has a plan before it is spent; a qualified adviser could help with bigger savings choices.

qa.q: How might Ma and Baba feel about the new line?
qa.a: They would likely feel cared for and relieved to have regular help with medicines and repairs 🙂

grounding: It shows sisters getting a salary rise and, instead of raising spending, rewriting the plan into more savings, a small upgrade and a fund for their parents.

subtype: Approach: revising categories after an income change [Revision]
passage:
Jahnavi burst into the flat waving a phone. "Yamini, I got it! The promotion came through!"
"Finally! Okay, where are we celebrating, and what are you buying?"
"That's the thing. My first thought was a new scooter. My second was a better flat. Then I looked at our shared plan, and I got nervous."
"Nervous? About more money?"
"Remember last time? I got a raise and three months later I was broke again. I just spent more."
"True. You bought that massage chair."
"Don't. So this time I'm splitting it before it lands. Most of the increase goes to savings. A little is for me: the scooter, but second-hand. And a fixed amount goes home to Amma every month; she's been paying for Appa's physio alone."
"That's... actually really grown-up. Can I borrow the plan?"
"Only if we celebrate with dosa, not a five-star."
"Deal."

qa.q: Where will the fixed amount go every month?
Why did Jahnavi feel nervous about the extra money?
qa.a: Jahnavi remembered spending the last raise and being broke three months later, so felt anxious about repeating it.

qa.q: What else could help Jahnavi stick with the split?
qa.a: Jahnavi could have the savings and Amma's amount move automatically on payday, and look at the plan with Yamini after three months.

qa.q: How does Yamini see Jahnavi's new plan?
qa.a: Yamini is impressed, calls it really grown-up, and even wants to borrow the plan.

grounding: It shows a young adult receiving a salary rise and, remembering the last one, rewriting the plan into more savings, a modest upgrade and support for the parents.
